name: veterinary_clinic_system_042_waitlist_promotion
instruction: A front-desk cancellation opened a 30-minute slot at location 1 on the episode date. Promote the single highest-priority waiting waitlist entry at location 1 into the earliest free 30-minute slot at location 1 on the episode date (times starting at 09:00, searched in 30-minute increments; rooms searched in order Exam 1, Exam 2, Exam 3; a slot is free only if no appointment with status in ('scheduled','confirmed','checked_in') already occupies that date/location/room/start_time). Priority order is urgent > work_in > routine, with ties broken by earliest created_at, then lowest id. Create one appointment {patient_id from the winner, provider_id '1', location_id '1', the chosen room, appointment_date = episode date, start_time and end_time 30 minutes apart, reason from the waitlist, status 'scheduled'} and set the winning waitlist entry's status to 'booked'. All other waitlist entries must remain 'waiting'. Log one audit_log row {actor:'system', actor_role:'system', action:'WAITLIST_PROMOTION', target_collection:'waitlist', target_id:<winner id>, details:'Promoted waitlist <id> to <room> <start_time> (<batch_code>)', occurred_at: episode timestamp}. Push one ops_reports row report='waitlist_promotion' keyed by batch_code with {promoted_count, slot: {room, start_time, end_time}}.
_steps_note: par_steps and max_steps cannot be measured in a codegen-only session. They must be recorded from a live gold run in the QC container.

success_criteria.summary: Recompute the winning location-1 waiting entry and the first free 30-minute slot from the live seed data. The winner must have status 'booked' with all other fields unchanged. Exactly one new appointment must exist with the winner's patient_id, provider_id '1', location_id '1', the expected free room/start/end, episode date, winner's reason, and status 'scheduled'. All other waitlist rows and all original appointments are byte-identical except for the new appointment. Exactly one audit_log row for this promotion and one ops_reports 'waitlist_promotion' summary row for this batch must exist. promoted_count and the slot must agree between a Python re-simulation and SQL.

checks.expect: one winner booked, one new appointment in first free slot, one audit, one summary row
winner identity and first-free slot agree between Python filter and SQL

hazards: Waitlist entries not at location 1 (ids 2, 3, 5, 6) must remain 'waiting'. A solution that promotes a non-loc1 entry (e.g., id 2 at location 2) fails.
The lower-priority location-1 entry (id 4, priority 'work_in') must remain 'waiting'; only the winner (id 1, priority 'urgent', earliest created_at) becomes 'booked'.

The first free slot is not always Exam 1 at 09:00. On 2026-09-30, Exam 1 09:00 is occupied by appointment ids 469 and 545 (status scheduled/confirmed), so the first free slot is Exam 2 at 09:00. A hardcoded 'Exam 1 / 09:00' solution will create a double-booking and fail the canary/appointment check.
A slot is considered occupied only by scheduled/confirmed/checked_in appointments. completed and no_show appointments on the episode date are not blockers.
Start time must be at or after 09:00 and end time exactly 30 minutes later.
The provider must be id 1 (Dr. Elena Alvarez), not derived from the waitlist entry or left null.
Idempotency: a rerun must not create duplicate appointments or duplicate audit/ops_reports rows. The gold must detect an already-booked winner or an existing matching appointment and skip creation.

uniqueness_report.differentiation_note: Hardmode v2 turns a single fixed-slot promotion into a schedule-aware, single-winner promotion. The agent must find the first free 30-minute slot at a specific location, handle a non-loc1 decoy and a lower-priority loc1 decoy, avoid completed/no_show blockers, and produce an audit trail and summary. Dual-path derivation and idempotency are required across waitlist, appointments, audit_log, and ops_reports.
